metadata.name: FEHM Engineering Ontology

baseline_metadata.description: Merged code-intelligence ontology combining the current ontology with the strict restore candidates.
baseline_metadata.merge_rule: Current ontology is the baseline; strict restore concepts are appended only when their exact concept name is not already present in the same section.

metadata.id_policy: IDs are immutable once released; labels and section membership may evolve. Prefixes record original assignment, not current taxonomy.
metadata.coverage: Broad engineering catalog; not an exhaustive dictionary or a validated detector implementation.

policy.findings: Never store repository findings in this catalog.
policy.evidence: Terminology mentions establish vocabulary use or documented claims, not implementation or achieved properties.
policy.absence: No evidence is unknown, not proof of absence.
policy.numeric_confidence: Not defined; do not synthesize scores.
policy.related_semantics: Symmetric or directional topical association only; no equivalence, causality, or detection implication.
policy.parent_semantics: Narrower concept within a broader engineering category; not a language subtype guarantee.
policy.retrieval_hints: OR candidate expansion seeds. Missing hints mean unspecified, not inapplicable.
policy.profile_inheritance: Effective detection is shared profile plus record-specific signals, anti_signals, and requirements; requirements are a union.
policy.evidence_scope: A finding must state observed surface: declaration, implementation, deployment, operation, measurement, or documented_claim.

evidence: resolved declaration, API contract, formal specification, or independently supported architecture explanation
signals: Bind a declaration or reference to the concept definition in its domain.
anti_signals: A matching term in a comment, identifier, or dependency name alone.
reference.limit: Documentation establishes a claim or vocabulary use; implementation and achieved properties require separate evidence.

evidence: equations, typed operations, algorithm bodies, or solver constraints
signals: Trace operands, update rules, and mathematical assumptions matching the definition.
anti_signals: Similar variable names or an unrelated math-library import.
math.limit: Approximate implementations and violated assumptions require explicit qualification.

evidence: parsed declarations, resolved symbols, type information, and compiler settings
signals: Match language-specific syntax and resolved semantics to the definition.
anti_signals: Unparsed text or shadowed identifiers.
language.limit: Dynamic dispatch, macros, generated code, and unsupported languages can leave results unknown.

evidence: resolved operations, loop updates, recursion, and control/data-flow slices
signals: Verify state representation, update steps, and termination conditions of the algorithm.
anti_signals: Name-only recognition or partial steps lacking algorithm invariants.
algorithm.limit: Worst-case complexity and equivalence need justified input and execution assumptions.

evidence: allocation/use/release flows, lifetime rules, and sanitizer or heap traces
signals: Trace ownership and storage lifetimes across aliases and cleanup paths.
anti_signals: Allocation alone does not establish a leak or unsafe access.
memory.limit: Feasibility, allocator behavior, and production frequency may require runtime evidence.

evidence: task creation, shared accesses, lock order, happens-before graph, and runtime traces
signals: Identify interacting execution contexts and their ordering or synchronization constraints.
anti_signals: Async syntax alone does not establish parallelism or a race.
concurrency.limit: Potential interleavings are static hypotheses unless feasibility or runtime observation is established.

evidence: resolved client/server calls, protocol handlers, network configuration, and packet traces
signals: Match protocol operations or settings to actual communication endpoints.
anti_signals: Unused client dependencies or protocol words in comments.
network.limit: Connectivity, negotiated security, and packet behavior require deployed or observed evidence.

evidence: DDL, migrations, query AST, transaction scopes, engine settings, and execution plans
signals: Resolve operations to actual database objects and relevant engine semantics.
anti_signals: ORM declarations or migration files not shown to be applied.
database.limit: Plans, isolation behavior, replication health, and speed depend on engine and deployment state.

evidence: cache get/set/invalidate paths, keys, TTLs, and backing-store operations
signals: Trace hit, miss, write, expiry, and concurrent-refresh paths.
anti_signals: Cache client construction without reachable cache operations.
cache.limit: Hit rate and stampede occurrence require workload observations; risk can be inferred structurally.

evidence: message flows, persistence boundaries, protocol state, topology, and failure traces
signals: Reconstruct participant roles, acknowledgment rules, and failure assumptions.
anti_signals: Multiple service classes or directories without independent process and communication evidence.
distributed.limit: An implemented mechanism does not prove global consistency, resilience, or availability.

evidence: resolved dependency graph, public interfaces, ownership, and deployment boundaries
signals: Check dependency direction and responsibility boundaries across components.
anti_signals: Folder names, architecture diagrams, or service count without corroboration.
architecture.limit: Architectural intent and implemented structure must be reported separately.

evidence: route or schema declarations, middleware order, handlers, and API client/server flows
signals: Trace request input through routing, validation, authorization, processing, and response.
anti_signals: Declared endpoint or annotation unreachable in the configured application.
api.limit: Contract declarations do not prove deployed behavior or compatibility with every consumer.

evidence: component tree, DOM/style rules, event handlers, browser traces, and accessibility tree
signals: Connect declarations to mounted components and user-observable behavior.
anti_signals: Unused components or accessibility attributes without usable interaction.
frontend.limit: Responsiveness, accessibility, and browser performance require representative runtime checks.

evidence: build manifests, IaC resources, pipeline graphs, rollout policies, and live state
signals: Resolve artifact production, promotion, resource references, and activation conditions.
anti_signals: Example manifests, disabled jobs, or unexecuted infrastructure plans.
deployment.limit: Declared desired state is not evidence that infrastructure is applied or healthy.

evidence: runbooks, incident records, probes, recovery exercises, and telemetry
signals: Connect stated procedure or target to dated operational evidence and scope.
anti_signals: Runbook presence does not establish execution or successful recovery.
operational.limit: Objectives, commitments, and observed outcomes are distinct claims.

evidence: metric definitions, units, aggregation windows, instrumented producers, and observations
signals: Identify numerator, denominator or quantile method, units, workload, and observation interval.
anti_signals: Metric names, dashboard labels, or instrumented counters without measured values.
metric.limit: Source may define measurement; actual values require observations and valid aggregation.

evidence: source-to-sink data flow, identity and policy checks, trust boundaries, and adversarial tests
signals: Trace attacker control, reachable sensitive actions, and intervening validation or authorization.
anti_signals: Security library presence or keyword matching without reachable flow.
security.limit: Potential vulnerabilities need reachability assumptions; absence of a finding is not a security guarantee.

evidence: test discovery, assertions, dependency seams, change graph, and repeated test outcomes
signals: Relate exercised behavior and test isolation to the relevant quality condition.
anti_signals: Test filenames alone or line coverage used as proof of correctness.
quality.limit: Quality judgments require scope and rationale; flakiness needs repeated outcomes under comparable inputs.

evidence: stage DAGs, schemas, transformations, checkpoints, and data-quality observations
signals: Trace source records through transformation, scheduling, and sink writes.
anti_signals: Pipeline or model class names without linked executable stages.
pipeline.limit: Data correctness, drift, model quality, and end-to-end freshness need representative datasets and observations.

evidence: prompt assembly, retrieval stages, model/tool calls, memory stores, and evaluation records
signals: Trace inputs, candidate selection, context construction, invocation, and output handling.
anti_signals: Model imports or prompts describing capabilities without executing them.
ai.limit: Groundedness, hallucination risk, retrieval quality, and agent success require task-specific evaluation.

evidence: topology, explicit failure model, workload telemetry, incident history, and recovery exercises
signals: Evaluate the property against a defined objective, interval, workload, and failure scope.
anti_signals: A supporting mechanism, replica, load balancer, or health check alone.
runtime-property.limit: Repository evidence supports design intent or hypotheses; achieved production properties are not source-verifiable.

evidence: formal contracts, engine semantics, proof obligations, or conformance tests
signals: Check guarantees and assumptions across every relevant operation boundary.
anti_signals: A guarantee asserted by naming or documentation alone.
formal-property.limit: General correctness and program equivalence are not decidable for arbitrary programs.

evidence: resource-flow slices, profiles, traces, benchmark inputs, and comparable measurements
signals: Relate a candidate cost or bottleneck to a representative workload and resource demand.
anti_signals: Nested loops, allocation, or external calls alone do not prove a production bottleneck.
performance.limit: Static analysis may identify risk; dominant cost and regressions require representative measurements.

evidence: parsed artifact contents and references from configured builds or execution paths
signals: Validate file format and resolve its consumers and declared semantics.
anti_signals: Filename extensions alone or sample artifacts excluded from active configuration.
artifact.limit: Existence, active use, and deployment are separate evidence levels.

concepts.definition: Repeated reads observe changed committed values during one transaction.

concepts.name: Phantom Read
concepts.definition: Repeated predicates return changed row sets within a transaction.

concepts.name: Throttling
concepts.definition: Restricting operation intensity through delay, admission, or reduced processing rate.

signals: Admission, delay, or scheduling logic reduces processing intensity under a stated condition.
anti_signals: Rate metrics without enforcement.

concepts.name: Entry Point
concepts.definition: Location where execution enters an application or subsystem.

concepts.name: Execution Path
concepts.definition: One ordered route through executed program operations.

concepts.name: Call Chain
concepts.definition: An ordered sequence of nested or causally linked calls.

signals: Resolved ordered calls or trace frames preserving invocation order.
anti_signals: A whole call graph does not identify a particular chain.

concepts.name: Dependency Chain
concepts.definition: An ordered path through dependency relationships.

concepts.name: Module Boundary
concepts.definition: Interface and visibility rules separating a module from others.

concepts.name: Code Path
concepts.definition: A possible route through a program's control flow.

concepts.name: Hot Path
concepts.definition: Code executed frequently or dominating a measured workload cost.

signals: Representative profile attributes high execution frequency or cost to a code region.
anti_signals: A frequently named method or loop alone.

concepts.name: Cold Path
concepts.definition: Code infrequently executed under a specified workload.

signals: Representative coverage or profiles show rare execution for a defined workload.
anti_signals: No observed execution does not imply unreachable code.

concepts.name: Helper Function
concepts.definition: Function supporting another operation through a focused subtask.

concepts.name: Shared Utility
concepts.definition: Reusable support functionality consumed by multiple components.

concepts.name: Orchestration Layer
concepts.definition: Layer coordinating the order and interaction of operations.

concepts.name: Integration Layer
concepts.definition: Layer adapting communication with external systems.

concepts.name: Application Layer
concepts.definition: Layer coordinating use cases and application workflows.

concepts.name: Domain Layer
concepts.definition: Layer representing business rules, domain state, and invariants.

concepts.name: Infrastructure Layer
concepts.definition: Layer implementing technical adapters and external resource access.

concepts.name: Source of Truth
concepts.definition: Authority used to resolve the correct value or state.

concepts.name: Single Source of Truth
concepts.definition: One authoritative representation governs a defined fact or decision.

concepts.name: Data Flow
concepts.definition: Propagation and transformation of values between program operations.

concepts.name: Execution Flow
concepts.definition: Ordering and coordination of program activities across execution contexts.

concepts.name: Event Lifecycle
concepts.definition: Stages from event creation through delivery, processing, and retention.

concepts.name: State Transition
concepts.definition: Change from one modeled state to another under conditions.

concepts.name: State Machine
concepts.definition: Behavior modeled by states, events, and permitted transitions.

concepts.name: Short-Circuit Evaluation
concepts.definition: Skipping remaining operands when an expression result is determined.

concepts.name: Happy Path
concepts.definition: Expected successful execution without exceptional conditions.

concepts.name: Error Path
concepts.definition: Execution responding to an operation failure or invalid condition.

concepts.name: Exceptional Path
concepts.definition: Control flow entered through exceptional runtime conditions.

concepts.name: Fallback Path
concepts.definition: Alternative execution used when the preferred operation is unavailable.

concepts.name: Retry Path
concepts.definition: Execution route that attempts a failed operation again.

concepts.name: Blocking Operation
concepts.definition: Operation preventing its execution context from progressing while waiting.

concepts.name: Non-Blocking Operation
concepts.definition: Operation allowing its execution context to progress without waiting inline.

concepts.name: Synchronous Execution
concepts.definition: Execution where completion is awaited before the caller continues.

concepts.name: Asynchronous Execution
concepts.definition: Execution whose completion is coordinated separately from invocation.

concepts.name: Deferred Execution
concepts.definition: Scheduling computation for a later evaluation point.

concepts.name: Annotations
concepts.definition: Metadata attached to program declarations for tooling or runtime interpretation.

concepts.name: Decorators
concepts.definition: Wrappers or transformations applied to declarations or callable objects.

concepts.name: Microtask
concepts.definition: Queued job processed at designated checkpoints before later event-loop tasks.

concepts.name: Macrotask
concepts.definition: Common browser term for an event-loop task scheduled outside the microtask queue.

concepts.name: Map Operation
concepts.definition: Applying a transformation independently to collection elements.

concepts.name: Filter Operation
concepts.definition: Selecting collection elements satisfying a predicate.

concepts.name: Reduce Operation
concepts.definition: Combining collection elements through an accumulating operation.

concepts.name: Break Statement
concepts.definition: Control transfer exiting an enclosing loop or supported selection construct.

concepts.name: Continue Statement
concepts.definition: Control transfer advancing to the next iteration of an enclosing loop.

concepts.name: Tight Coupling
concepts.definition: Interdependence making components difficult to change independently.

signals: Change co-occurrence, unstable interface dependencies, and cross-boundary implementation knowledge.
anti_signals: High call count alone.

concepts.name: Loose Coupling
concepts.definition: Interaction through limited stable contracts reducing change propagation.

concepts.name: High Cohesion
concepts.definition: Responsibilities within a component strongly support a common purpose.

signals: Responsibilities and data access align with a shared capability and invariants.
anti_signals: Small file size alone.

concepts.name: Low Cohesion
concepts.definition: A component combines responsibilities with little shared purpose.

concepts.name: Circular Dependency
concepts.definition: Dependency cycle complicating initialization, layering, or independent change.

signals: Cycle in resolved import, module, build, or runtime dependency graph with edge types stated.
anti_signals: Textual imports unresolved by language/package rules.

concepts.name: Transitive Dependency
concepts.definition: Dependency reached indirectly through another dependency.

concepts.name: Dependency Boundary
concepts.definition: Defined limit governing permitted dependencies between components.

concepts.name: Upstream Dependency
concepts.definition: Provider or prerequisite relative to a declared dependency direction.

concepts.name: Downstream Dependency
concepts.definition: Consumer or dependent relative to a declared dependency direction.

concepts.name: Shared Dependency
concepts.definition: Provider required by multiple consuming components.

concepts.name: Dependency Leakage
concepts.definition: Implementation dependencies exposed through an intended abstraction boundary.

concepts.name: Hidden Dependency
concepts.definition: Required state or service absent from an explicit interface contract.

signals: Ambient globals, service lookup, process state, or implicit I/O absent from declared contract.
anti_signals: Every private helper automatically called hidden.

concepts.name: Architectural Boundary
concepts.definition: Constraint separating responsibilities, dependencies, ownership, or deployment scopes.

concepts.name: Service Boundary
concepts.definition: Contract and ownership scope defining a service's responsibilities.

concepts.name: Service Decomposition
concepts.definition: Partitioning system capabilities into separately scoped services.

concepts.name: Control Plane
concepts.definition: Components configuring and coordinating system behavior.

concepts.name: Data Plane
concepts.definition: Components performing primary data movement or request processing.

concepts.name: Stateful Service
concepts.definition: Service retaining relevant state across independent interactions.

concepts.name: Stateless Service
concepts.definition: Service not retaining required client-specific state between interactions.

concepts.name: Blast Radius
concepts.definition: Scope of impact reachable from a failure or compromise.

signals: Dependency and trust graphs bound the reachable impact of a specified failure.
anti_signals: Reachability alone proves all reachable nodes will fail.

concepts.name: Failure Domain
concepts.definition: Resources sharing a correlated failure exposure.

concepts.name: Bottleneck
concepts.definition: Resource or stage constraining overall performance under a workload.

concepts.name: Scaling Bottleneck
concepts.definition: Constraint preventing capacity growth as resources or demand increase.

concepts.name: Architectural Trade-off
concepts.definition: Choice balancing competing system qualities under constraints.

concepts.name: Leaky Abstraction
concepts.definition: Abstraction requiring consumers to understand hidden implementation details.

signals: Consumer branches on provider internals or imports implementation-only types.
anti_signals: An interface exposing intentional documented semantics.

concepts.name: Accidental Complexity
concepts.definition: Complexity introduced by implementation choices rather than inherent requirements.

concepts.name: Architectural Erosion
concepts.definition: Implementation progressively diverging from intended architectural constraints.

concepts.name: Data Model
concepts.definition: Representation of data entities, relationships, constraints, and semantics.

concepts.name: Data Integrity
concepts.definition: Data remains accurate and consistent with declared invariants.

concepts.name: Data Ownership
concepts.definition: Responsibility and authority over a dataset's semantics and lifecycle.

concepts.name: Read Model
concepts.definition: Representation optimized for answering queries.

concepts.name: Write Model
concepts.definition: Representation enforcing state changes and write-side invariants.

concepts.name: Query Path
concepts.definition: Sequence of operations used to resolve a query.

concepts.name: Read Path
concepts.definition: Sequence retrieving and preparing stored data for a consumer.

concepts.name: Write Path
concepts.definition: Sequence validating, recording, and persisting an update.

concepts.name: Transaction Boundary
concepts.definition: Scope within which operations share transaction guarantees.

concepts.name: Full Table Scan
concepts.definition: Reading all table rows to evaluate a query.

concepts.name: Hot Key
concepts.definition: Key receiving disproportionate traffic and creating concentrated load.

signals: Per-key workload distribution concentrates requests or contention on an identified key.
anti_signals: Static common key literal alone.

concepts.name: Data Locality
concepts.definition: Proximity of computation to required data or memory locations.

concepts.name: Data Migration
concepts.definition: Moving or transforming stored data between representations or systems.

concepts.name: Stale Data
concepts.definition: Observed data older than required freshness or consistency expectations.

concepts.name: Duplicate Records
concepts.definition: Multiple records representing the same intended logical fact.

concepts.name: Idempotent Write
concepts.definition: Repeated equivalent writes have one intended logical effect.

concepts.name: Eventual Convergence
concepts.definition: Replicated state approaches agreement after updates cease and communication succeeds.

concepts.name: Latency Bottleneck
concepts.definition: Stage dominating response delay for a specified workload.

concepts.name: Throughput Bottleneck
concepts.definition: Stage limiting completed work per unit time.

concepts.name: p95 Latency
concepts.definition: Latency value at or below which 95 percent of observations fall.

concepts.name: p99 Latency
concepts.definition: Latency value at or below which 99 percent of observations fall.

concepts.name: Memory Pressure
concepts.definition: Memory demand approaches capacity and triggers costly management behavior.

concepts.name: CPU-Bound Workload
concepts.definition: Workload whose progress is primarily limited by CPU computation.

concepts.name: I/O-Bound Workload
concepts.definition: Workload whose progress is primarily limited by input-output operations.

concepts.name: Allocation Overhead
concepts.definition: Time or resource cost attributable to memory allocation and reclamation.

concepts.name: Serialization Overhead
concepts.definition: Time or resources spent converting data representations.

concepts.name: Network Overhead
concepts.definition: Communication cost beyond the application's useful computation or payload.

concepts.name: Query Latency
concepts.definition: Elapsed time to execute and return a query result.

concepts.name: Cache Miss Rate
concepts.definition: Fraction of cache accesses not satisfied by retained entries.

concepts.name: Warm Start
concepts.definition: Startup reusing previously initialized resources or cached state.

concepts.name: Batching
concepts.definition: Grouping operations to amortize fixed processing or communication costs.

concepts.name: Connection Reuse
concepts.definition: Using an established connection for additional operations.

concepts.name: Contention
concepts.definition: Competing work delays access to a shared resource.

concepts.name: Lock Contention
concepts.definition: Concurrent tasks compete for the same synchronization lock.

concepts.name: Thread Contention
concepts.definition: Threads compete for shared execution or application resources.

concepts.name: Performance Regression
concepts.definition: A change worsens performance under a comparable measured workload.

signals: Comparable before/after workloads show worsened resource or timing distributions.
anti_signals: Changed code shape without measurement.

concepts.name: Head-of-Line Blocking
concepts.definition: Delayed work prevents later independent work from progressing.

concepts.name: Coordinated Omission
concepts.definition: Measurement underreports latency by omitting requests during stalls.

concepts.name: Amdahl's Law
concepts.definition: Parallel speedup is limited by the fraction of serial work.

concepts.name: Little's Law
concepts.definition: Stable average population equals arrival rate multiplied by average time in system.

concepts.name: Utilization
concepts.definition: Fraction of resource capacity actively used during a defined interval.

concepts.name: Working Set
concepts.definition: Data or memory actively required during a workload interval.

concepts.name: Cache Pollution
concepts.definition: Low-value entries evict useful cached data.

concepts.name: Middleware Pipeline
concepts.definition: Ordered middleware stages surrounding request handling.

concepts.name: Routing Layer
concepts.definition: Component selecting application handlers from request attributes.

concepts.name: Response Serialization
concepts.definition: Converting response values into the transport representation.

concepts.name: Contract Mismatch
concepts.definition: Producer and consumer expectations disagree about an interface contract.

concepts.name: Schema Mismatch
concepts.definition: Data shape or types disagree with an expected schema.

concepts.name: Forward Compatibility
concepts.definition: Older consumers tolerate intended future producers or extensions.

concepts.name: Integration Boundary
concepts.definition: Contract and trust boundary between interacting systems.

concepts.name: Third-Party Dependency
concepts.definition: Externally owned software or service required by the application.

concepts.name: Webhook Delivery
concepts.definition: Sending event notifications to registered HTTP receivers.

concepts.name: Callback Flow
concepts.definition: Execution coordinated by invoking registered continuation functions.

concepts.name: Request Correlation
concepts.definition: Associating related requests and telemetry across components.

concepts.name: Authentication Flow
concepts.definition: Sequence establishing, validating, and maintaining an identity claim.

concepts.name: Authorization Check
concepts.definition: Evaluation of permission for a concrete action and resource.

concepts.name: Error Propagation
concepts.definition: Transfer of failure information through calls or message boundaries.

concepts.name: Apache Kafka
concepts.definition: Distributed event platform using partitioned durable logs and consumer groups.

signals: Resolved Kafka clients, broker configuration, topic partitions, and producer/consumer calls.
anti_signals: Kafka word in documentation or unused dependency.

concepts.name: Trust Boundary
concepts.definition: Boundary across which data or actors have different trust assumptions.

signals: Source or actor identity crosses a point with changed control, privileges, or validation assumptions.
anti_signals: A network hop with unchanged trust assumptions.

concepts.name: Privilege Boundary
concepts.definition: Boundary separating operations with different permission levels.

concepts.name: Tenant Isolation
concepts.definition: Prevention of unauthorized interference or data access between tenants.

signals: Tenant-scoped queries, caches, object storage, and authorization tested across tenant identities.
anti_signals: Tenant column or header alone.

concepts.name: Input Trust
concepts.definition: Assumptions about input provenance, control, and validation requirements.

signals: Input provenance and attacker influence mapped to validations before sensitive uses.
anti_signals: Internal network location automatically trusted.

concepts.name: Secret Exposure
concepts.definition: Sensitive secret material becomes accessible outside its intended scope.

concepts.name: Credential Leakage
concepts.definition: Authentication material escapes its authorized handling boundary.

concepts.name: Token Lifecycle
concepts.definition: Issuance, use, renewal, expiration, and revocation of security tokens.

concepts.name: Authorization Bypass
concepts.definition: Access succeeds without satisfying the required permission policy.

signals: Feasible path reaches a protected action without satisfying its required policy.
anti_signals: Missing local decorator when enforcement may be upstream.

concepts.name: Insecure Default
concepts.definition: Default configuration permits unnecessary or unsafe exposure.

concepts.name: Injection Surface
concepts.definition: Input paths capable of reaching interpreted command or code contexts.

concepts.name: Security Invariant
concepts.definition: Security condition required to hold across allowed state transitions.

concepts.name: Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use
concepts.definition: State changes between validation and dependent use invalidate the safety decision.

concepts.name: Confused Deputy
concepts.definition: Privileged component misuses its authority for an insufficiently authorized requester.

concepts.name: Capability Security
concepts.definition: Authority conveyed through unforgeable references to permitted operations.

concepts.name: Cryptographic Agility
concepts.definition: Ability to replace algorithms or keys without redesigning the system.

concepts.name: Artifact Attestation
concepts.definition: Verifiable statement about an artifact and its production or assessment.

concepts.name: Reproducible Dependency Resolution
concepts.definition: Declared inputs resolve to consistent dependency identities across builds.

concepts.name: Data Residency
concepts.definition: Data location constrained by organizational or jurisdictional requirements.

concepts.name: Purpose Limitation
concepts.definition: Processing personal data only for defined compatible purposes.

concepts.name: Test Seam
concepts.definition: Point where behavior or collaborators can be replaced during testing.

concepts.name: Test Isolation
concepts.definition: Tests avoid unintended interference from shared state or environments.

concepts.name: Regression Surface
concepts.definition: Existing behavior potentially affected by a change.

concepts.name: Brittle Test
concepts.definition: Test coupled to incidental details and failing under harmless changes.

concepts.name: Mock-Heavy Testing
concepts.definition: Testing style relying extensively on substituted collaborators.

concepts.name: Edge Case
concepts.definition: Uncommon input or state requiring special consideration.

concepts.name: Boundary Condition
concepts.definition: Input or state at the limit of a valid partition.

concepts.name: Untested Path
concepts.definition: Execution path lacking evidence of test exercise.

concepts.name: Test Coverage Gap
concepts.definition: Relevant program elements or behaviors missing test exercise.

concepts.name: Regression Risk
concepts.definition: Potential for a change to break previously working behavior.

concepts.name: Fragile Abstraction
concepts.definition: Interface whose consumers break under small implementation changes.

signals: Small internal changes repeatedly force unrelated consumer changes, supported by history or tests.
anti_signals: Aesthetic judgment without supporting change evidence.

concepts.name: Dead Code
concepts.definition: Code that cannot contribute to relevant observable behavior.

signals: Reachability and data-flow analysis show no relevant observable contribution under explicit roots.
anti_signals: Missing test coverage mistaken for dead code.

concepts.name: Unreachable Code
concepts.definition: Code for which no feasible execution path exists under assumptions.

signals: No feasible incoming control-flow path under stated execution roots and assumptions.
anti_signals: Static call graph omits reflective or generated targets.

concepts.name: Duplicate Logic
concepts.definition: Equivalent business or implementation rules maintained in multiple places.

concepts.name: Cognitive Complexity
concepts.definition: Measure of control-structure difficulty under a stated scoring method.

concepts.name: Mutation Score
concepts.definition: Fraction of nonexcluded injected mutants detected by tests.

concepts.name: Fault Localization
concepts.definition: Identifying program locations likely responsible for observed failures.

concepts.name: Minimal Reproduction
concepts.definition: Smallest practical example retaining a reported failure.

concepts.name: Delta Debugging
concepts.definition: Systematically minimizing failure-inducing inputs or changes.

concepts.name: Test Oracle
concepts.definition: Mechanism deciding whether observed behavior is acceptable.

concepts.name: Semantic Diff
concepts.definition: Change representation emphasizing program meaning rather than text alone.

concepts.name: Deployment Artifact
concepts.definition: Versioned output packaged for installation or execution.

concepts.name: Deployment Unit
concepts.definition: Smallest set of components released or rolled back together.

concepts.name: Environment Parity
concepts.definition: Relevant development, test, and production conditions remain comparable.

concepts.name: Infrastructure Drift
concepts.definition: Provisioned resources diverge from declared infrastructure state.

concepts.name: Release Gate
concepts.definition: Condition required before a release advances.

concepts.name: Rollout Strategy
concepts.definition: Plan controlling how a release reaches users or instances.

concepts.name: Immutable Artifact
concepts.definition: Published artifact identified by content or version cannot change in place.

concepts.name: Deployment Dependency
concepts.definition: Prerequisite ordering or compatibility constraint between releases.

concepts.name: Secret Injection
concepts.definition: Supplying secrets to workloads at controlled execution boundaries.

concepts.name: Resource Limit
concepts.definition: Enforced upper bound on workload resource consumption.

concepts.name: Autoscaling Trigger
concepts.definition: Observed condition causing resource-count adjustment.

concepts.name: Operational Runbook
concepts.definition: Actionable procedures for routine operations and incident response.

concepts.name: Startup Probe
concepts.definition: Check allowing startup completion before liveness enforcement.

concepts.name: Pod Disruption Budget
concepts.definition: Policy limiting voluntary disruption of Kubernetes workload availability.

concepts.name: Grace Period
concepts.definition: Bounded interval allowing in-progress work to finish before termination.

concepts.name: Deployment Freeze
concepts.definition: Temporary restriction on releases during elevated operational risk.

concepts.name: Expand-Contract Migration
concepts.definition: Compatibility-preserving migration adding new structure before removing old structure.

concepts.name: Feature Flag Debt
concepts.definition: Accumulated obsolete or complex feature controls increasing maintenance risk.

concepts.name: Toil
concepts.definition: Repetitive operational work that scales with service growth and has little lasting value.

concepts.name: Operational Readiness Review
concepts.definition: Assessment of service supportability before production operation.

concepts.name: Certificate Expiry
concepts.definition: Certificate passes its validity interval and may prevent trusted communication.

concepts.name: Root Cause
concepts.definition: Causal factor whose removal would prevent a defined failure under stated assumptions.

concepts.name: Contributing Factor
concepts.definition: Condition increasing incident likelihood, severity, or duration.

concepts.name: Symptom
concepts.definition: Observable effect indicating a possible underlying problem.

concepts.name: Trace Context
concepts.definition: Identifiers and metadata linking operations within a distributed trace.

concepts.name: Incident Timeline
concepts.definition: Ordered evidence of incident events, decisions, and interventions.

concepts.name: Error Rate
concepts.definition: Fraction or frequency of failed operations under a defined denominator.

concepts.name: Saturation
concepts.definition: Extent to which a resource exceeds or approaches useful capacity.

concepts.name: Latency Distribution
concepts.definition: Distribution of elapsed operation times over a defined population.

concepts.name: Alert Fatigue
concepts.definition: Excessive alerts reduce attention and effective response.

concepts.name: Noisy Alert
concepts.definition: Alert frequently firing without a useful actionable condition.

concepts.name: Observability Gap
concepts.definition: Missing evidence preventing understanding of relevant system behavior.

concepts.name: Missing Instrumentation
concepts.definition: Relevant operations lack required telemetry production.

concepts.name: Incident Mitigation
concepts.definition: Action reducing ongoing incident impact.

concepts.name: Remediation
concepts.definition: Change correcting an identified defect or harmful condition.

concepts.name: Recurrence Prevention
concepts.definition: Changes reducing the probability of a similar future incident.

concepts.name: Ingestion Pipeline
concepts.definition: Coordinated stages receiving and preparing external content.

concepts.name: Retrieval Pipeline
concepts.definition: Stages selecting, filtering, and ranking information for a task.

concepts.name: Embedding Pipeline
concepts.definition: Stages preparing inputs and producing indexed vector representations.

concepts.name: Context Assembly
concepts.definition: Selecting and arranging evidence and instructions for a model request.

concepts.name: Context Window Utilization
concepts.definition: Fraction of available model context consumed by supplied and generated tokens.

concepts.name: Retrieval Quality
concepts.definition: Fitness of retrieved evidence for the downstream information need.

signals: Labeled query set, relevance judgments, and downstream answer evaluation.
anti_signals: Vector similarity scores treated as correctness.

concepts.name: Context Recall
concepts.definition: Fraction of required reference evidence represented in retrieved context under a rubric.

signals: Labeled required facts are matched against context under a documented relevance rubric.
anti_signals: Model confidence interpreted as evidence recall.

concepts.name: Grounding
concepts.definition: Connecting generated claims to verifiable supplied or retrieved evidence.

signals: Each asserted claim links to evidence supporting its actual meaning.
anti_signals: Citation presence alone.

concepts.name: Hallucination Risk
concepts.definition: Potential for unsupported or false generated claims under a task setting.

concepts.name: Prompt Composition
concepts.definition: Combining instructions, variables, examples, and evidence into a prompt.

concepts.name: Inference Bottleneck
concepts.definition: Resource or stage constraining model inference performance.

concepts.name: Tool Execution Flow
concepts.definition: Sequence from tool selection through invocation, result handling, and continuation.

concepts.name: State Persistence
concepts.definition: Retaining application state beyond an individual execution lifetime.

signals: Writes to a durable state store and recovery on a later execution.
anti_signals: In-memory dictionary alone.

concepts.name: Conversation Memory
concepts.definition: Retained interaction information used in subsequent dialogue turns.

concepts.name: Inference Latency
concepts.definition: Elapsed time for a specified model inference operation.

concepts.name: Model-Serving Bottleneck
concepts.definition: Serving component limiting model request capacity or responsiveness.

concepts.name: Prompt Cache Invalidation
concepts.definition: Discarding reusable prompt results when relevant inputs or policies change.

concepts.name: Retrieval Precision
concepts.definition: Fraction of retrieved items judged relevant under an evaluation rubric.

concepts.name: Retrieval Recall
concepts.definition: Fraction of known relevant items retrieved under an evaluation rubric.

concepts.name: Context Precision
concepts.definition: Fraction of supplied context judged useful for the specified answer task.

concepts.name: Evidence Deduplication
concepts.definition: Collapsing repeated evidence while preserving distinct provenance and meanings.

concepts.name: Token Counting
concepts.definition: Measuring encoded token length using a specified tokenizer and serialization.

concepts.name: Context Overflow
concepts.definition: Assembled context exceeds the model's permitted token capacity.

concepts.name: Evaluation Contamination
concepts.definition: Evaluation examples leak into training or development decisions.

concepts.name: Tool Output Injection
concepts.definition: Untrusted tool output attempts to redirect model behavior or authority.

concepts.name: Tool Permission Boundary
concepts.definition: Limit on actions permitted through an agent's external tools.

concepts.name: Agent Loop Limit
concepts.definition: Bound on agent steps, time, expenditure, or tool invocations.

concepts.name: Embedding Version Drift
concepts.definition: Indexed and query embeddings use incompatible representations or model versions.

concepts.name: Index Freshness
concepts.definition: Delay between authoritative source change and searchable index update.

concepts.name: Retrieval Abstention
concepts.definition: Declining a supported conclusion when retrieved evidence is insufficient.

concepts.name: Local-First Architecture
concepts.definition: Primary data processing and user control remain available locally.

concepts.name: Selective Context Retrieval
concepts.definition: Fetching only task-relevant knowledge and evidence within a bounded context budget.

concepts.name: Evaluation Harness
concepts.definition: Infrastructure executing evaluation cases and recording comparable outcomes.

signals: Executable case discovery, scorer invocation, and comparable result recording.
anti_signals: Evaluation instructions in a prompt alone.

concepts.name: Prefill
concepts.definition: Model processing of input tokens to construct state before autoregressive decoding.

concepts.name: Decode Phase
concepts.definition: Iterative generation of output tokens using the model's accumulated state.

concepts.name: Classification Precision
concepts.definition: True positives divided by predicted positives under a specified class convention.

concepts.name: Classification Recall
concepts.definition: True positives divided by actual positives under a specified class convention.

concepts.name: F1 Score
concepts.definition: Harmonic mean of precision and recall under a specified averaging convention.

concepts.name: ROC AUC
concepts.definition: Area under the true-positive versus false-positive rate curve across thresholds.

concepts.name: PR AUC
concepts.definition: Area under a precision-recall curve under a specified integration convention.

concepts.name: Mean Absolute Error
concepts.definition: Mean absolute difference between predictions and reference values.

concepts.name: Root Mean Squared Error
concepts.definition: Square root of mean squared prediction error.

concepts.name: Train-Serving Skew
concepts.definition: Differences between training and serving feature computation degrade model behavior.

concepts.name: Feature Freshness
concepts.definition: Age of feature values relative to their required observation time.

concepts.name: Algorithm
concepts.definition: Finite description of steps for solving a specified class of problems.

concepts.name: Computability
concepts.definition: Whether a problem can be solved by an effective procedure.

concepts.name: Decidability
concepts.definition: Existence of an algorithm terminating with an answer for every input.

concepts.name: Halting Problem
concepts.definition: Undecidable general problem of determining whether a program terminates.

concepts.name: Turing Machine
concepts.definition: Abstract computational model with state, tape, and transition rules.

concepts.name: Invariant
concepts.definition: Condition preserved across specified operations or state transitions.

concepts.name: Precondition
concepts.definition: Condition required before an operation is valid.

concepts.name: Postcondition
concepts.definition: Condition guaranteed after successful operation completion.

concepts.name: Loop Invariant
concepts.definition: Condition preserved across iterations and used to reason about a loop.

concepts.name: Termination
concepts.definition: Computation eventually reaches a completed state under assumptions.

concepts.name: Correctness
concepts.definition: Behavior satisfies a specified contract under stated assumptions.

concepts.name: NP-Complete
concepts.definition: Decision problems both in NP and NP-hard under stated reductions.

concepts.name: Polynomial Time
concepts.definition: Running time bounded by a polynomial in input size.

concepts.name: Graph Degree
concepts.definition: Number of incident edges under a specified direction convention.

concepts.name: Bipartite Graph
concepts.definition: Graph whose vertices split into two sets with only cross-set edges.

concepts.name: Weighted Graph
concepts.definition: Graph assigning numeric weights to edges or vertices.

concepts.name: Topological Ordering
concepts.definition: Linear vertex order respecting all directed acyclic dependencies.

concepts.name: Numerical Conditioning
concepts.definition: Sensitivity of a mathematical problem's output to input perturbations.

concepts.name: Bias-Variance Trade-off
concepts.definition: Balance between systematic model error and sensitivity to training samples.

concepts.name: Statistical Power
concepts.definition: Probability of rejecting a false null under a specified alternative.

concepts.name: Multiple Testing
concepts.definition: Inference across many hypotheses requiring joint error consideration.

concepts.name: Covariance
concepts.definition: Type constructor preserves a subtype relation between its arguments.

concepts.name: Contravariance
concepts.definition: Type constructor reverses a subtype relation between its arguments.

concepts.name: Invariance
concepts.definition: Type constructor permits neither covariant nor contravariant substitution in a position.

concepts.name: Best-Case Complexity
concepts.definition: Minimum resource cost over inputs of a given size under a specified model.

concepts.name: Average-Case Complexity
concepts.definition: Expected resource cost under a declared input probability distribution.

concepts.name: Worst-Case Complexity
concepts.definition: Maximum resource cost over inputs of a given size under a specified model.

concepts.name: Symbol Identity
concepts.definition: Stable identity of a declared or inferred program entity.

concepts.name: Reference Resolution
concepts.definition: Connecting uses of program names to their definitions.

concepts.name: Points-to Analysis
concepts.definition: Approximating objects or locations referenced by pointer values.

concepts.name: Alias Analysis
concepts.definition: Determining whether expressions may refer to the same storage.

concepts.name: Interprocedural Analysis
concepts.definition: Program analysis spanning function-call boundaries.

concepts.name: Intraprocedural Analysis
concepts.definition: Program analysis confined to one procedure.

concepts.name: Path Sensitivity
concepts.definition: Analysis distinguishes facts along different control-flow paths.

concepts.name: Flow Sensitivity
concepts.definition: Analysis distinguishes facts at different program positions.

concepts.name: Context Sensitivity
concepts.definition: Analysis distinguishes different calling contexts.

concepts.name: Soundness
concepts.definition: Analysis includes every behavior allowed by its explicit semantic assumptions.

concepts.name: Precision
concepts.definition: Analysis avoids unnecessary overapproximation under its abstraction.

concepts.name: Analysis Unsoundness
concepts.definition: Analysis omits possible behaviors within its claimed scope.

concepts.name: Incremental Analysis
concepts.definition: Recomputing only facts affected by changed inputs or dependencies.

concepts.name: Dynamic Call Target
concepts.definition: Potential callee selected using runtime values or dispatch.

concepts.name: Generated Code
concepts.definition: Code produced by tools rather than directly maintained as the source of truth.

concepts.name: Vendored Dependency
concepts.definition: External dependency stored within the repository tree.

concepts.name: Architecture Conformance
concepts.definition: Implemented dependency structure satisfies declared architectural constraints.

concepts.name: Evidence Provenance
concepts.definition: Origin, extraction method, revision, and assumptions supporting an analysis claim.

concepts.name: Repository Fingerprint
concepts.definition: Compact description of detected languages, dependencies, and build artifacts.

concepts.name: Change Impact Analysis
concepts.definition: Estimating affected behavior and dependencies from a proposed change.

concepts.name: Language Fingerprint
concepts.definition: Evidence-backed identification of a programming language from parsed files and build metadata.

concepts.name: Build Graph
concepts.definition: Dependency graph of build targets, actions, and generated artifacts.

concepts.name: Reachability Root
concepts.definition: Entry point or externally callable entity assumed reachable by an analysis.

concepts.name: Analysis Coverage
concepts.definition: Portion of relevant repository entities supported and analyzed under stated semantics.

concepts.name: Unsupported Construct
concepts.definition: Program construct an analyzer cannot interpret within its declared model.

concepts.name: Ambiguous Symbol
concepts.definition: Reference with multiple unresolved or plausible binding targets.

concepts.name: Source Revision
concepts.definition: Identifier of the exact source state underlying an analysis result.

concepts.name: Hard Real-Time Deadline
concepts.definition: Missing a specified execution deadline constitutes system failure.

concepts.name: Soft Real-Time Deadline
concepts.definition: Late completion degrades value without necessarily invalidating overall operation.

concepts.name: Worst-Case Execution Time
concepts.definition: Upper execution-time bound under a specified hardware and execution model.

concepts.name: Interrupt Latency
concepts.definition: Delay between an interrupt event and handler execution.

concepts.name: Hardware Abstraction Layer
concepts.definition: Interface isolating hardware-specific operations from application logic.

concepts.name: Direct Memory Access
concepts.definition: Hardware transfer of data without CPU movement of each element.

concepts.name: Memory-Mapped I/O
concepts.definition: Hardware registers accessed through processor address-space operations.

concepts.name: End-to-End Safety Case
concepts.definition: Structured argument and evidence supporting a system safety claim.

concepts.name: Geospatial Coordinate Reference System
concepts.definition: Definition mapping spatial coordinates to physical locations.

concepts.name: Spatial Join
concepts.definition: Combining records according to spatial relationships.

concepts.name: Multi-Region Data Residency
concepts.definition: Regional placement and movement of data satisfy defined location constraints.

concepts.name: Conflict-Free Offline Sync
concepts.definition: Synchronizing disconnected edits using explicit conflict-resolution semantics.

concepts.name: Payment Reconciliation
concepts.definition: Comparing payment records with authoritative external settlement evidence.

concepts.name: Double-Entry Ledger
concepts.definition: Recording balanced debit and credit entries for each financial transaction.

concepts.name: Scientific Reproducibility
concepts.definition: Independent execution can recover stated results from declared methods and inputs.

concepts.name: Experiment Provenance
concepts.definition: Recorded inputs, versions, configuration, and procedures of an experiment.

concepts.name: Accessibility Tree
concepts.definition: Semantic interface representation exposed to assistive technology.

concepts.name: Desktop IPC Bridge
concepts.definition: Controlled communication boundary between desktop application processes.

concepts.name: Mobile Offline Sync
concepts.definition: Reconciling local mobile state with remote state after disconnection.
